memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If anyone dedicates to the LORD part of their family land, its value is
to be set according to the amount of seed required for it - fifty shekels
of silver to a homer of barley seed. If they dedicate a field during the
Year of Jubilee, the value that has been set remains'" - Lev 27:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now the vow reaches a family's land — and in an agricultural society,
land was everything. It was your income, your security, your inheritance,
the source of your daily bread. To dedicate a field to the Lord was to
place your very livelihood in His hands.

The value was measured by how much seed the field required, tied to the
Jubilee cycle we saw in the previous chapter. Everything was accounted
for fairly and carefully.

Dear reader, notice the progression through this chapter. It began with
persons, moved to animals, then to a house, and now to the land that
provided a living. God's people were invited to bring even their means of
income and lay it before Him.

This touches a sensitive nerve for most of us. We may sing about
surrendering everything, but our work, our earnings, our financial
security — these we tend to keep firmly in our own control.

Jesus said where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Matt
6:21). He was not against us having possessions; He was warning that our
possessions can quietly come to possess us.

What would it mean to genuinely place your livelihood in God's hands — to
hold your career, your income, your security as things dedicated to Him
rather than clutched for yourself? It is often the last area we surrender,
and the one that most reveals where our trust truly lies.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I surrendered my livelihood and finances to God, or kept them
   back?
2. Where has my treasure quietly captured my heart?
3. What would it look like to hold my income as dedicated to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, I place my work, my income and my security in Your hands. Free my
heart from clutching them, and help me trust You as my true provider.
Amen.
